reply.text:
All module files transform cleanly with 200s and no parse errors, and I've exercised the live server directly with the exact payloads the form sends (success → `{"id":900}`, invalid quantity → `422 {"errors":{"quantity":...}}`, invalid customer → `422 {"errors":{"customer":...}}`), confirming the response shapes match what `OrderForm.tsx` and `orders.http.ts` expect.

**Summary of what was built:**
- `services/orders.contract.ts` — `OrdersApi` interface (`customers`, `createOrder`), `OrderRejected` error carrying field messages.
- `services/orders.http.ts` — real `fetch` adapter against `/api/customers` and `/api/orders` (this app has a live server, unlike the devices fixture).
- `services/orders.context.ts` — `useOrdersApi()`, same pattern as `useDeviceApi()`.
- `modules/orders/orders.validation.ts` (+ test) — pure client-side validation (customer required, quantity integer 1–1000, note ≤200 chars).
- `modules/orders/orders.queries.ts` — `useCustomers()` query, `useCreateOrder()` mutation.
- `modules/orders/OrderForm.tsx` — the form: `data-testid="order-form"`, per-field errors (`error-customer`/`error-quantity`/`error-note`) shown before sending and merged with server 422 errors, submit button (`data-testid="submit"`) disabled while pending, success clears the form and shows `data-testid="created"` with the new id.
- Wired into `main.tsx` and `styles/global.css`.

Lint, typecheck, and all 27 tests (including the new validation tests) pass. One caveat: I could not visually verify the rendered form in a browser — no `chromium-cli` or Playwright is available in this sandbox and there's no network to install one — so I verified correctness through direct API calls against the real server plus static/type verification instead. If you want an actual visual check, let me know and I can walk you through installing a browser driver, or you can check it yourself at `http://127.0.0.1:59219`.
